title: Where should feature flags be evaluated?
context: A public HTTP API and its web client need per-account flags. Flags change without a redeploy, assignment stays consistent across two regions, and peak traffic is 8k requests per second.

recommendation.reason: Keep request context and latency local; share fixtures between the Go and TypeScript evaluators so parity is testable.

options.title: Evaluate inside each service
options.summary: Load rules from the config service and evaluate in-process per request.
options.rationale: Request context is already present, and the decision stays next to the code that uses it.
options.tradeoff: Two evaluator implementations must agree on bucketing and defaults.
cons: Two SDKs to keep in parity

options.title: Evaluate at the edge
options.summary: Push rules to edge workers and decide before requests reach origin.
options.rationale: One evaluation point serves every region and runtime without changing service code.
options.tradeoff: The edge sees less context and adds a platform dependency to the request path.

options.title: Precompute assignments in a background job
options.summary: Write per-account assignments to a low-latency store that services read.
options.rationale: Evaluation leaves the request path and every runtime reads the same plain values.
options.tradeoff: Assignments lag rule changes and storage grows with accounts × flags.

note: SAMPLE fixture: same generic static decision as live mode.
